title: Grouped comparison of fixed versus evolving basket-node effective hydraulic resistance
scientific_question: Does a fixed effective-resistance representation adequately predict the qualified Waszkiewicz pressure-flow-mass response across held-out physical brews and controlled conditions, or is one bounded evolving-resistance component justified?

authority.pressure: line pressure measured; basket-node pressure derived by fitted brewer-loss subtraction
authority.mass: scale measured then aligned and interpolated
authority.time: retain exact source synchronization and sample cadence

frozen_candidate_model_family.W-H5: simple observation-delay alternative only where source semantics justify it

modeling_strategy: Directly predict a qualified pressure, flow, or mass channel or vector under the source forcing and observation structure; use threshold-controlled apparent resistance only as a diagnostic.
fairness: no complete held-out-brew fitting presented as prediction
prefer the simpler model within uncertainty
primary_metric: prospectively frozen condition-balanced held-out predictive error on a direct qualified channel or vector of channels

outcomes.positive: Authorize the smallest EWP-compatible evolving-resistance component task after stable grouped predictive advantage.
outcomes.negative: Preserve fixed hydraulic resistance and use the source to constrain uncertainty and benchmark ranges.
outcomes.null: Retain the simpler model and quantify the detectable effect threshold.
outcomes.blocked: Perform one bounded source-observation qualification; do not default to home-lab collection.

relationships.visualizer: Population operating envelopes and future representative boundaries; not a replacement for this controlled decision.
relationships.wadsworth_vaca: Potential later separate priors and observation operators for translating effective resistance into parameter distributions.
relationships.home_laboratory: No home-lab work is needed for the source-internal comparison.
